analysis.title: People Inc. (PPLI) Q3'26 Review: Focused on Transformation of Publishing Assets & Capital Allocation
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on PPLI and cuts the 12-month price target to $56 from $63, based on lower operating estimates after the Q3'26 print and forward commentary. Price was $36.88, implying 51.8% upside.
Core sessions fell 26% YoY in Q3'26 as AI search pressure and Google AI Overview penetration grew. Session-based revenue declined 6% YoY.
Non-session-based revenue rose 15% YoY, driven by Licensing & Other revenue up 49% on content licensing, AI-related partnerships and Apple News+ distribution.
Emerging & Other revenue rose 21% YoY. The Daily Beast grew 39% and Vivian Health grew 18%, accelerating from 12% in Q2.
Print revenue fell 16% YoY, reflecting portfolio optimization and the shift of advertising dollars from print to digital.
Management lowered its FY26 Digital growth outlook to +MSD% and reiterated that 2027 should return to +MSD-HSD% YoY Digital growth on easier comps.

Management is targeting a ~$45mm run-rate corporate overhead saving by the end of Q1'27, and signaled a return to share repurchases funded by recent asset monetization while staying opportunistic on M&A.

GS says the near-term stock driver is the visibility and trend of Digital growth, specifically search traffic pressure against the pace of non-session revenue growth. Capital allocation (MGM stake value, exits of non-core assets, M&A, buybacks) is the second driver over the next 3-6 months.
GS lowers 2027 revenue to $1.83bn (from $1.86bn) but raises 2027 Adj. EBITDA to $337m (from $331m) and GAAP EPS to $1.22 (from $1.11), on lower corporate costs.
Q4'26 estimates are cut: revenue $521m (from $527m), Adj. EBITDA $132m (from $139m), GAAP EPS $0.55 (from $0.67). FY26 GAAP EPS is now $(2.80) versus $6.24 before.

The sum-of-the-parts values People Inc. at 6.5x EBITDA (from 6.0x), Emerging & Other at 2.0x sales, the MGM stake at market price ($2,080m), and Turo at $380m, then applies a 10% tax/liquidity discount to reach $56 per share.

The text and Exhibit 1 conflict. The negatives section says People Inc. revenue and Adj. EBITDA missed GSe/Street, but Exhibit 1 shows total Adj. EBITDA of $56m against GS $46m and consensus $41m, and People Inc. Adj. EBITDA of $73m against GS $66m and consensus $61m.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated, price target cut from $63 on lower operating estimates after Q3'26. GS sees SOTP upside from the operating businesses, the MGM stake, Turo and capital returns.

earnings_insights: PPLI Q3'26 reported 11/3 (Exhibit 1, actual vs GS vs consensus): revenue $437m vs $436m GS vs $434m consensus. Adj. EBITDA $56m vs $46m GS vs $41m consensus. Gross margin 64.2% vs 63.8% GS vs 66.5% consensus.
Q3'26 segment Adj. EBITDA (reported): People Inc. $73m vs $66m GS vs $61m consensus. Emerging & Other $3m vs $2m. Corporate $(20)m vs $(22)m GS.

The text's negatives section says People Inc. revenue and Adj. EBITDA came in below GSe/Street on weaker advertising and search traffic, which conflicts with the exhibit. Management lowered the higher end of FY26 Adj. EBITDA guidance.

GS estimates (not reported): Q4'26E revenue $521m, Adj. EBITDA $132m, GAAP EPS $0.55. 2027E revenue $1.83bn, Adj. EBITDA $337m, GAAP EPS $1.22. 2028E revenue $1.90bn, Adj. EBITDA $378m, GAAP EPS $1.70.
FY26E GAAP EPS is $(2.80) versus the prior $6.24 estimate. Q3'26 core sessions were down 26% YoY and Print revenue down 16% YoY, both reported.
risk_factors: Emergence of competitors in each of People Inc.'s businesses.
Competitive impact of AI-generated answers on the ability to monetize digital publishing properties.
Rate of decline in Print People Inc. revenue.
A decline in the share price of MGM, which is valued at market price in the SOTP.
Disruption in the advertising landscape or a slowdown in broader macroeconomic conditions.

tension_points.bull_case: Management reiterated a return to +MSD-HSD% YoY Digital growth in 2027 on easier comps. Non-session revenue rose 15% YoY in Q3'26, with Licensing & Other up 49%. GS sees SOTP upside to $56 with a buyback restart and cost cuts.
tension_points.bear_case: Core sessions fell 26% YoY in Q3'26 on AI search pressure and Google AI Overview penetration, driving session-based revenue down 6%. FY26 Digital growth was lowered to +MSD% and the higher end of FY26 Adj. EBITDA guidance was cut.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 2027 Digital growth failing to return to the +MSD-HSD% YoY range that management reiterated.

theme_stances.key_argument: Easier 2027 comps, scaling of non-session revenue and capital allocation support SOTP upside despite AI search pressure on sessions.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to see compelling value in PPLI shares
